subject: rhat and priors for derived parameters

messages.author: 0ee8ae7c0d185529
messages.subject: rhat and priors for derived parameters
parts:
Dear all,

I am running a relatively simple path and coded some derived parameters to estimate indirect effects - for example A := B*C, where A, B, and C are specified in the equations as per lavaan syntax.  Everything converges fine, but I noticed that the output does not give the rhats or the list of priors for these derived parameters.  Is that intended?

Thanks

David

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: rhat and priors for derived parameters
parts:
David

That is how its supposed to work. As the derived parameters are a function of the estimated parameters, they are not "estimated" parameters, but "calculated" from the other posteriors. For the same, you have priors for the estimated parameters, but not the calculated ones
This is equivelant to do calculations outside of the blavaan estimation with the posteriors. blavInspect(fit, "mcmc").
A principle of posterior distributions is that as long as the parameters have converged, you can do calculations based on the estimated posteriors.

Hope this helps

messages.subject: Re: rhat and priors for derived parameters
parts:
Yes, if you were to export the mcmc draws and calculate the derived parameters that way, you will get the same posteriors. But if you add it into the syntax, it will already be there and exported as a parameter by blavaan.

Based on this principle of calculations based on posterior draws we can add a bunch of features, like the fit indices from blavFitIndices()

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: rhat and priors for derived parameters
parts:
Hi David,

Adding to what Mauricio said, here is a bit of a detailed reply about rhat.

For target="jags" and also "stanclassic" (I think), you do get rhat and effective sample size in the summary output.

The target="stan" (the default) is a little different. The Stan model is compiled once when you install blavaan (as opposed to every time you try to fit a model), and it is tough to anticipate every defined parameter that a person would request. So, for summary output, the posterior mean and SD of defined parameters are actually computed via the delta method, using the posterior distributions of the parameters involved in the definition.

You could instead compute the posterior yourself, as Mauricio said, by extracting the posterior samples. If you do that, you should probably run parTable() and look at the pxnames column, because those names will correspond to the column names of the posterior samples. And then the monitor() function from rstan will compute rhat and neff for you, if you have the posterior samples organized in the right way.

About priors for defined parameters: those are tricky. Consider your example A := B*C. If B has a normal prior and C has a normal prior, then the implied prior for A is a product of normals. And it gets trickier as more parameters become involved on the right side. blavaan will not be able to tell you anything there.

Best,
Ed
